A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PAKs play distinct roles in axon guidance and P cell migration, and that MAX-2 and PAK-1 are required for UNC-5 signaling during VCCMN axon guidance.
MAX-2 is required in parallel with the PAK-1/rac pathway to function downstream of the UNC receptor UNC-6/netrins during commissural axonal guidance.
MAX-2 and PAK-1 are required for axon guidance and are functionally redundant for P cell migration, but are differentially required during axon guidance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C. elegans UNC-6/netrins and the C. elegand PAKs are differentially required during axon guidance.
PAK-1 and max-2 are differentially required during axon guidance and that max-2 functions downstream or in parallel to PAK-1 in a rac-independent manner.
PAKs are required for axon guidance in both vertebrate and invertebrate systems, and that the C. elegans MAX-2 and PAK-1 are functionally redundant for axon guidance of both P cells and VCCMNs.
